context: hygienic process & CIP-led · HACCP / food-safety sign-off

brief.intro: New to this project type? A food & beverage processing plant turns raw ingredients into packaged food, dairy or beverage product through hygienic process lines — mixing, cooking or pasteurising, filling and packaging — built to washdown and food-safety standards. Unlike a normal industrial building, the building fabric itself is a food-safety system: hygienic walls, floors and drainage falls must be right before equipment moves in. Clean-in-Place (CIP) systems that automatically wash the process line without disassembly, and hygiene-zone HVAC that keeps contamination out of open-product areas, are the schedule drivers. The facility is only handed over once it passes a HACCP / food-safety audit, not just mechanical completion.

scope.desc: Power distribution, PLC/SCADA line control, hygiene-zone HVAC controls.

scope.name: Testing & commissioning
scope.desc: Line commissioning, CIP validation, and HACCP / food-safety sign-off — the real handover gate.

must_get_right: It's hygiene-led — building fabric, piping slope/finish and drainage are food-safety systems, not cosmetic; get the falls and coving right before equipment moves in.
CIP systems must be commissioned and validated before any product-contact run — treat CIP proving as a hard predecessor to process trials, not parallel scope.
Sequence utilities (steam, refrigeration, process water) ahead of process-line commissioning — a cold-chain or steam gap stops the wet trial.
Protect the HACCP / food-safety sign-off — it is the real handover gate, not mechanical completion; leave real time for the audit and any corrective actions.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. CIP validation and HACCP sign-off are scheduled as real-duration, deliverable-based activities rather than zero-duration milestones.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Civil and structure run a 6-day week; hygienic fabric and process-equipment installation run controlled single/double shift to protect finish quality; CIP validation and wet trials often run to a fixed, continuous calendar once started so cycle testing is not interrupted mid-run.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: The driving path runs hygienic envelope & fabric → process equipment & sanitary piping → utilities (steam/refrigeration) & CIP systems → line (mechanical) commissioning → CIP validation → product-representative wet trial → HACCP / food-safety sign-off. Hygienic fabric — drainage falls, coving, washdown finishes — must be complete and clean before equipment installation to avoid re-cleaning or rework.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Design is frozen and equipment vendor drawings issued before foundation/piping design; utilities (steam, refrigeration, process water) are available by the CIP-proving milestone; a single validation campaign; the food-safety authority inspection is scheduled after the wet trial.

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Hygienic areas require controlled, gowned access from fabric completion onward; sanitary-welding (orbital weld / passivation) crews are a specialist, constrained resource; the wet trial and HACCP audit need production, QA/food-safety and maintenance teams on site together.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Principal risks: sanitary-piping weld/passivation rework, CIP validation failures (coverage or temperature) requiring re-test, and HACCP audit findings extending sign-off. Schedule contingency is held before CIP validation and before the food-safety audit, not spread across construction.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for fabric/piping works and CIP/wet-trial execution — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
